inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted, net of the 94.24m shares held by TML Benefit Trust (eliminated as treasury in the consolidated accounts). 889.0m is the diluted weighted count implied by Q2 FY2027 (PAT 15,860 / diluted EPS 17.84); FY2026 annual note: 887.78m diluted including 1.36m dilutive options. Held FLAT because SBC is expensed in the flows. PRE-BONUS basis: the 1:1 bonus issue recommended with Q2 FY2027 results had not gone ex at price_as_of (price still on the pre-bonus scale, inside the 52-week range). When it goes ex, the share count doubles and every per-share value here halves; nothing else changes.
inputs.reported_fcf_basis: Operating cash flow 61,720 less capex 6,957 = 54,763 (the Metrics CSV figure), less lease cash 5,789 (repayment of lease liabilities 4,638 in financing + interest expense on lease liability 1,151) = 48,974. Lease cash is taken out here because Ind AS 116 puts it in financing; see lease_treatment.
inputs.interest_income_note: Net cash is ~1.5x owner FCF, so the double-count rule applies, but nothing is deducted: the Ind AS cash flow statement already removes interest income (980) and fair-value gains on treasury investments (1,539) from operating cash flow and shows interest received under investing. Reported FCF therefore carries no return on the cash pile. Deducting 980 again would strip it twice.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2026 annual report, consolidated statement of cash flows: 'Share Based Payments to Employees' 963 (FY2025: 686). Indian ESOPs are not net-share settled, so there is no equity-award tax line (EquityAwardTaxes = 0 throughout).
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-11-13T09:58:09Z NSE regular-session close (Friday); ex the Rs 15 interim dividend, pre the 1:1 bonus
inputs.balance_sheet_note: Cash and investments 73,300 is the 30 Sep 2026 figure from the Q2 FY2027 release (Rs 7,330 crore). The quarterly releases carry no balance sheet, so borrowings (696) are the 31 Mar 2026 audited figure; they were 4,714 a year earlier and are immaterial. Lease liabilities (21,166 at 31 Mar 2026) are excluded from net debt under lease treatment B.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in INR, the currency of the flows: India 10-year G-sec ~6.6% + beta ~0.9 x India equity risk premium ~6.0% = cost of equity ~12.0%. Borrowings are negligible, so WACC = cost of equity. Beta sits above TCS's ~0.8 because a third of revenue is telecom, tied to carrier capex. In line with the folder's other INR-built IT services models (TCS.NS 11.5%, HCLTECH.NS 12.0%, WIT 11.5%). The same 12.0% is used in all three scenarios: risk is charged once, in the probability-weighted flows. Terminal growth 5% INR nominal = ~2-3% USD growth plus ~2-3% structural INR depreciation.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment B, leases as operating cost. Lease cash (principal 4,638 + lease interest 1,151 = 5,789, 1.02% of FY2026 revenue) is charged inside the flows through lease_cost_pct_path; lease liabilities are excluded from net debt; D&A is taken ex right-of-use depreciation (18,816 total less 5,121 ROU = 13,695, 2.41% of revenue) so the lease is not charged twice. The EBITDA margin path is therefore the reported post-Ind-AS-116 EBITDA margin plus the 0.17% SBC add-back; model EBIT runs ~0.15pp below reported EBIT.
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are 100% consolidated; NCI profit share is nil (FY2026: -54 on PAT of 48,109). The NCI stock is deducted once, at 31 Mar 2026 book value (4,616), in the equity bridge.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, component build, with the non-US adaptations (INR-built WACC, single lease treatment, NCI charged once). Routed as an operating company: IT services and BPS, value is a free cash flow stream, no lending book. First valuation of this ticker. CURRENCY: statements are in INR millions and the NSE quote is INR (Yahoo meta currency INR), so no FX bridge. SBC is small but real (0.17% of revenue) and is kept as an explicit line; no buybacks since FY2020 (17,879), so the flat count is a modelling convention funded by the SBC charge rather than by repurchases. Dividends carry the capital return (payout ~85% of profit). TIMING: FY0 is FY2026 and year 1 is FY2027, of which H1 is already reported (revenue 318,920, +16.6% YoY in INR; EBIT margin 14.4% then 14.8%). The 30 Sep cash balance already holds H1 FY2027 free cash flow (~28bn, ~31/share) which year 1 counts again; against that, year 1 is discounted a full twelve months when FY2027 ends in 4.5 months, which understates value by roughly 7%. The two are left unadjusted and the net effect is conservative. INR TRANSLATION: USD/INR moved from ~84 to ~95 through FY2026-H1 FY2027; about 10pp of the 16.6% H1 INR growth is translation, not volume (USD revenue +6.5%). The year-1 growth figure carries that one-off and later years do not. TML BENEFIT TRUST: the trust's 94.24m shares (9.6% of issued capital) are treated as treasury, consistent with the consolidated EPS denominator; no asset is added for them. The Metrics KPI 'FreeCashFlowUSD Q4 FY2026 = 616' looks like the full-year figure filed under the quarter (FY2026 FCF of 54,763 is ~USD 616m); not used here.

equity_bridge.item: Interim dividend declared Oct 2026, paid after the 30 Sep balance sheet
equity_bridge.note: Rs 15/share x 885.6m shares outstanding net of trust. Price is ex-dividend (Yahoo ex-date 23 Oct 2026) but the 30 Sep cash balance still holds the money.

FY2026 AR consolidated balance sheet note 40B: amounts claimed by 37 companies as alleged advances to erstwhile Satyam, carried as a liability since 2009. Deducted in full as a debt-like claim; conservative, ~14/share.
Total equity incl. NCI 300,770 less owners' equity 296,154 at 31 Mar 2026.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: revenue_5yr_cagr, trimmed; equity CAGR rejected (see warning)
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5-year CAGR (3.6%) is less than half the revenue 5-year CAGR (8.5%). Book value is not a growth signal here: the company pays out ~85% of profit as dividends, so equity barely compounds. EPS is flat over both windows because FY2024 margins collapsed to ~6% EBIT and FY2026 has only just recovered FY2021-23 earnings.
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGRs are on the owner series: operating cash flow less capex, less SBC, less lease principal (FY2026 49,162; FY2023 40,281; FY2021 69,154). Lease interest is excluded from the historical series because it is not available for every year; it is included in the FY2026 base (last_fcf). The negative 5-year FCF CAGR is a base effect: FY2021 FCF (74,278 reported) was a pandemic working-capital release, nearly double FY2020 and FY2022. SBC is ~2% of FCF and is not growing faster than cash flow. FY2019 has no cash flow or balance sheet row in the Metrics CSV.

base.growth_note: Year 1 (FY2027): H1 is reported at +16.6% in INR; H2 assumed ~+11.5% as the rupee comparison base catches up. Thereafter ~6% USD growth as the USD 4bn+ of trailing deal wins converts, plus ~2.5% rupee depreciation, fading to 5.5%.
base.margin_note: Reported EBIT margin 14.8% in FY2027 (H1 14.6%, the Fortius ~15% target reached on exit), 15.2% in FY2028 and 15.5% from FY2029, held there. That still leaves TechM the lowest-margin large Indian IT exporter. EBITDA path = reported EBIT + D&A ex-ROU + lease cash + SBC - 0.15.
base.capex_note: FY2026 capex was 1.22% of revenue; 1.5% adds an allowance for the bolt-on acquisitions the company makes most years (899 and 1,620 in the last two).
base.tax_note: FY2026 cash taxes 16,502 were 25.1% of pre-tax profit; book rate 26.9%. No loss shelter or one-off to ramp out.
base.wc_note: Negative: receivables and unbilled revenue (DSO 88 days) exceed payables and unearned revenue, so growth consumes cash. FY2026 working capital absorbed 14,872 on 38,271 of added revenue, inflated by rupee revaluation of USD receivables; 15% of incremental revenue is the normalised rate.

bull.margin_note: Reported EBIT margin 15.0% in FY2027 rising to 17.5% by FY2030, roughly where HCLTech and Wipro sit; still well short of Infosys and TCS.

bear.margin_note: Reported EBIT margin 14.3% in FY2027, then back to 12.5% by FY2030 (the FY2026 level): half the Fortius gain is given back, not the whole of it.

scenario_narratives.base: The turnaround lands and then stops improving. FY2027 closes at about the 15% EBIT margin management has promised since FY2024, helped by a rupee that fell from ~84 to ~95 per dollar. The record deal wins (four straight quarters above USD 1bn, trailing twelve months above USD 4bn) convert into about 6% dollar growth, which with normal rupee depreciation is 8-9% in INR, fading to 5.5%. Telecom stays near a third of revenue and roughly flat; manufacturing, BFSI and healthcare carry the growth. Margin settles at 15.5%, because the cost programme is largely spent and H-1B fees and wage inflation absorb what operating leverage adds. Owner FCF margin runs about 10-11%.
scenario_narratives.bull: Deal wins convert at the rate their size implies and TechM grows with or ahead of the top tier for the first time in a decade: 8% in dollars, 10-11% in INR for four years. Diversification takes telecom below 28% of revenue, and the telecom book itself turns up on agentic network operations work. Margin keeps climbing past the Fortius target on revenue leverage and offshore mix, reaching 17.5% EBIT by FY2030, the level HCLTech and Wipro already earn. This needs both growth and margin to deliver together, which TechM has not managed in any year since FY2019.
scenario_narratives.bear: The deal wins turn out to be renewals and vendor-consolidation swaps at lower prices, so TCV rises and revenue does not: dollar growth falls back to 1-2%, as it was through FY2024-26, and INR growth to ~4% once the currency tailwind laps. A carrier capex cut or the loss of a top-five telecom client hits the third of revenue that is still communications. With the cost levers used, AI-driven price deflation on run work, the USD 100,000 H-1B fee and wage inflation push EBIT margin back to 12.5% by FY2030. The business stays cash generative and net cash, so this is a de-rating case, not a solvency one; terminal value is on Gordon at 4%, well above the zero floor.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 25%, above the 15% house default: three years of margin gains have come from cost cuts while dollar revenue grew under 2% in FY2026, and a third of revenue rests on one cyclical vertical. Base 50%: H1 FY2027 already shows 6.5% dollar growth and a 14.8% margin, so the guidance-year anchors are largely in hand. Bull 25%, below the 35% default: it needs deal conversion and continued margin expansion together, and the company has no record of delivering both in the same year.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Tech Mahindra is valued as a mature, net-cash IT services business whose margin recovery is mostly complete. The flows are owner FCF after SBC and after lease cash, in INR, discounted at an INR-built 12%. The market price pays for more than the base case delivers: it needs either the bull margin path (17%+ EBIT) or a required return of about 9.5% in INR (see the required-return table). The question for an owner is whether record deal wins become revenue; margin alone is already in the price.
key_risks_to_valuation: Deal-win conversion: TCV is up ~40% while FY2026 dollar revenue grew 1.9%. Year 2-5 growth is the largest single driver of the gap between bear and bull.
Margin durability once Project Fortius cost levers are exhausted; each 1pp of terminal EBIT margin is worth roughly 6-7% of value.
Rupee path: about 10pp of FY2027 INR growth is translation. A rupee recovery would reverse part of it and trim margin by ~25-30bp per 1%.
Telecom concentration (~32% of revenue) and carrier capex cycles.
Discount rate: the valuation is in INR at 12%; at 11% the base value rises by roughly 17%.
Per-share scale: the 1:1 bonus issue will halve all per-share figures when it goes ex. Compare like with like.
